name: Question 7
problem: A particle $P$ of mass $2\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude $2{e}^{-t}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing $x,$ and $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the change in kinetic energy of the particle between the times $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,s$ and $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,s.$
worked_solution:
The change in kinetic energy of a particle with mass $m,$ initial velocity ${v}_{0},$ and final velocity ${v}_{1}$ is given by

$$
Δ\,\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2}.
$$

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules ($J$).

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\int 2{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =-2{e}^{-t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
0=-2{e}^{-0}+C\,⟹\,C=2.
$$

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2-2{e}^{-t}.$ In particular, its inital velocity at time $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,s$ and final velocity at time $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,s$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{0} & =v(\operatorname{ln}⁡2)=2-2{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡2}=1\,m/s, \\ {v}_{1} & =v(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)=2-2{e}^{-\operatorname{ln}⁡4}=\frac{3}{2}\,m/s.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the change in kinetic energy of the particle between these times is

$$
\begin{aligned}Δ\,\text{KE} & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}m{v}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot {(\frac{3}{2})}^{2}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot {(1)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9}{4}-1 \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\,J.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 7
?

A particle P of mass 2kg moves along the x-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude 2e−tm/s2, where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing x, and t≥0 is the time in seconds. Calculate the change in kinetic energy of the particle between the times t=ln⁡2s and t=ln⁡4s.

a
3J
b
54J
c
4J
d
2J
e
32J
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The change in kinetic energy of a particle with mass m, initial velocity v0, and final velocity v1 is given by ΔKE=12mv12−12mv02.

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules (J).

First, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time: v(t)=∫a(t)dtv(t)=∫2e−tdtv(t)=−2e−t+C

To determine C, we use the fact that v(0)=0. Substituting this into the above gives 0=−2e−0+C⟹C=2.

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time t is v(t)=2−2e−t. In particular, its inital velocity at time t=ln⁡2s and final velocity at time t=ln⁡4s are v0=v(ln⁡2)=2−2e−ln⁡2=1m/s,v1=v(ln⁡4)=2−2e−ln⁡4=32m/s.

Therefore, the change in kinetic energy of the particle between these times is ΔKE=12mv12−12mv02=12⋅2⋅(32)2−12⋅2⋅(1)2=94−1=54J.
